title: The Lantern Keeper
text: An old woman with a lantern stands where the path should fork, though you cannot see a fork. She will light your way, she says, for a memory. She is smiling at the most haunted of you, who has memories they would gladly lose.

options.label: Let the most haunted trade her a memory for the light, glad to be rid of it.

outcomes.text: Afterward they cannot recall their mother's face. The path ahead is short and well lit; they tell themselves the price was fair.
She takes more than she said, smiling all the while. The path is short and lit, yet they cannot remember why they are crying.

options.label: Refuse her and find your own way in the dark. Your memories are your own.

outcomes.text: You find it, eventually, after a night of walking in circles past the same dead tree.
At the end of your path you find her waiting with her lantern dark. Something stands in the shadows behind her.
While you search, something else finds you in the dark where her light does not reach.
